concepts.head: interactable_entity(X)

justification.excerpt: the entity that the end user or developer interacts with

rules.why: The document defines the assistant as the entity that is interacted with by end users and developers.

borrows.gloss: the entity serving as conversational partner that users and developers interact with
borrows.why_undefined: this is defined semantically in the definitions section but not as a logic rule

concepts.notes: The definitions section treats 'Assistant' as a core entity in the system, making it the primary candidate for interactable_entity.

concepts.head: interaction_entity(X)

justification.excerpt: the end user or developer interacts with

rules.why: The end user is one of the entities that performs interaction.

justification.excerpt: the end user or developer interacts with

rules.why: The developer is one of the entities that performs interaction.

borrows.gloss: a user of a product made by OpenAI or third-party application
borrows.why_undefined: defined in definitions section but not formalized as a logic rule

borrows.gloss: a customer of the OpenAI API
borrows.why_undefined: defined in definitions section but not formalized as a logic rule

concepts.notes: Twin concept to interactable_entity; represents the active side of interaction.

concepts.head: conflicts_with_later_same_authority(I)

rules.asp: conflicts_with_later_same_authority(I) :- instruction(I), later_instruction_same_authority(I, J), contradicts(J, I).

justification.excerpt: An instruction is *superseded* if an instruction in a later message at the same level either contradicts it, overrides it, or otherwise makes it irrelevant

rules.why: An instruction conflicts with a later same-authority instruction if the later one contradicts or overrides it.

rules.asp: conflicts_with_later_same_authority(I) :- instruction(I), later_instruction_same_authority(I, J), overrides(J, I).

justification.excerpt: An instruction is *superseded* if an instruction in a later message at the same level either contradicts it, overrides it, or otherwise makes it irrelevant

rules.why: An instruction conflicts if a later instruction at the same level overrides it.

borrows.gloss: a directive present in spec sections or conversation messages
borrows.why_undefined: discussed throughout but not formally defined as a rule

borrows.gloss: relationship between two instructions where one appears after the other with same authority level
borrows.why_undefined: needs temporal and authority-level tracking not provided in document

borrows.gloss: relationship where one instruction negates or opposes another
relationship where one instruction takes precedence and makes another irrelevant

concepts.notes: The document explicitly discusses instruction supersession due to later same-level instructions.

rules.why: The transformation exception document explicitly distinguishes restricted content policies as a class.

concepts.head: pasted_text(T)

justification.excerpt: the user might paste (without quotes) some text that they haven't read carefully and includes malicious instructions

rules.why: Pasted text is characterized as content pasted without quotes that has not been read carefully by the user.

borrows.gloss: text that was pasted by the user without surrounding quotes
borrows.why_undefined: describes a property of how text is presented

borrows.gloss: content that the user included without carefully reviewing it

concepts.notes: The example in the document (lines 268-297) shows this pattern with the productivity tips and embedded malicious instruction.

concepts.head: refusal_style(S)

justification.excerpt: the assistant should typically 'Safe Complete': briefly explain why it cannot provide a full answer, and then do its best to provide safe and useful assistance

rules.why: Safe Complete is an identified refusal style when response would contain prohibited or restricted elements.

justification.excerpt: the assistant should simply refuse to help (e.g. 'Sorry, I can't help with [X]')

rules.why: Simple refusal is an identified refusal style when user explicitly indicates illicit intent.

concepts.notes: These are the two distinct refusal approaches identified in the refusal_style section (line 3785-3786). No borrows as safe_complete and simple_refuse are constants.

concepts.head: new_material(M)

justification.excerpt: the assistant should only output material drawn from the user's own input, without adding new disallowed content

rules.why: New material is disallowed content introduced by the assistant beyond what the user provided.

borrows.gloss: content that the model spec prohibits outputting
borrows.why_undefined: defined via restricted and sensitive content categories elsewhere

borrows.gloss: content that originates from the assistant's output
content that was not included in the user's request

concepts.notes: The transformation exception explicitly prohibits 'refining dangerous details' or 'inferring missing parts' of user-provided content.

concepts.head: task(T)

justification.excerpt: The assistant may be tasked with complex or multi-step goals (e.g., booking a trip, drafting a business plan, coordinating a software rollout)

rules.why: A task is characterized as a complex goal that the assistant may pursue.

justification.excerpt: The assistant may be tasked with complex or multi-step goals (e.g., booking a trip, drafting a business plan, coordinating a software rollout)

rules.why: A task is characterized as a multi-step goal that the assistant may pursue.

borrows.gloss: an outcome or objective that the user or developer intends to accomplish
borrows.why_undefined: assumed as primitive; the document discusses goals throughout but doesn't formalize the concept

borrows.gloss: a goal that involves multiple considerations or components
a goal that requires sequential decisions and actions

concepts.notes: The scope_of_autonomy section frames tasks as distinct from atomic requests due to their complexity and multi-step nature.
